problem:
What is the first term that is less than $0.000\,08$ in the following geometric sequence?

$$
256,\,64,\,16,\,4,\,…
$$
worked_solution:
The first term of the sequence is ${a}_{1}=256$ and the common ratio is

$$
r=\frac{64}{256}=\frac{1}{4}.
$$

So, the $n$th term of the sequence can be written as:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}\cdot {r}^{n-1} \\  & =256\cdot {(\frac{1}{4})}^{n-1} \\  & ={4}^{4}\cdot {4}^{1-n} \\  & ={4}^{5-n}\end{aligned}
$$

We want the $n$th term to be less than $0.000\,08.$
Hence:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & <0.000\,08 \\ {4}^{5-n} & <0.000\,08 \\ \operatorname{log}⁡({4}^{5-n}) & <\operatorname{log}⁡(0.000\,08) \\ (5-n)\operatorname{log}⁡(4) & <\operatorname{log}⁡(0.000\,08) \\ 5-n & <\frac{\operatorname{log}⁡(0.000\,08)}{\operatorname{log}⁡(4)} \\ -n & <\frac{\operatorname{log}⁡(0.000\,08)}{\operatorname{log}⁡(4)}-5 \\ n & >5-\frac{\operatorname{log}⁡(0.000\,08)}{\operatorname{log}⁡(4)}\end{aligned}
$$

Estimating the right-hand side using a calculator, we get:

$$
5-\frac{\operatorname{log}⁡(0.000\,08)}{\operatorname{log}⁡(4)}≈11.805
$$

Therefore, the $12$th term is the first term of the sequence that is less than $0.000\,08.$
